text:
This looks like early 2014. Unemployment was 6.7% in both December 2013 and March 2014. The 10-year yield was 2.71% and the 12-month change in the 10-year yield was +1.01 pp, which fits a month-end of about January 2014 (when it ended near 2.67%) or possibly December 2013 (3.04%). The 2-year yield at 0.44% fits March 2014 (0.44%).

Other cues point the same way:
- US large-cap equity returned +20.3% over 12 months. Over the 12 months to March 2014 it returned about 21%, and the S&P 500 was at its high.
- The 1-month equity return was +0.7%, and March 2014 was about +0.8%.
- Unemployment of 6.7% fits March 2014. The rate was 6.7% in December 2013, 6.6% in January and 6.7% in March, so a 3-month change of 0.0 fits March.
- Headline CPI of 1.5% fits March 2014.
- Gold's 12-month return of -13% fits March 2014. Gold was down about 14% over that period.

The 10-year yield ended March 2014 at about 2.72%, which matches. The snapshot is March 2014.
